### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_003_BEGIN -->
Yes, consuming too much protein can be harmful for muscle growth as excess protein intake can lead to an increase in calorie consumption, which can result in weight gain and excess body fat. Additionally, consuming excessive protein can also cause kidney damage or increase the risk of dehydration. It is important to balance protein intake with other nutrients like carbohydrates and fats, and to consult with a healthcare professional or registered dietitian to determine an appropriate and safe amount of protein intake for individual needs and goals.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_003_END -->

### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_005_BEGIN -->
Protein supplements can certainly help in muscle growth during weightlifting, especially for individuals who struggle to get enough protein from whole food sources alone. Protein supplements such as whey, casein, or plant-based powders can be convenient and efficient ways to increase protein intake. However, it is important to note that whole foods provide other important nutrients like vitamins, minerals, and fiber that are also essential for good health. Therefore, it is recommended to get most of the daily protein requirement from whole foods and use protein supplements as an adjunct when necessary. A combination of nutrient-dense whole foods and protein supplements can help support muscle growth during a weightlifting program.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_005_END -->
